QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_43

question.text: Tax-free bonds issued under Section 10 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, offer:

answer.text: Complete exemption of interest income from tax

explanation.text: The Logic: Tax-free bonds offer complete tax exemption on interest income under Section 10 of the Income Tax Act. The interest received by the bondholder is entirely exempt from income tax. The Trap: This is different from tax-saving bonds which offer deduction under Section 80C. Tax-free bonds exempt the interest income itself, not the investment amount. Cross-Exam Context: Tax treatment of different fixed income instruments is tested in Series IV and extensively in Series V-A (mutual fund taxation). Distributor's Pro-Tip: Tax-free bonds are typically issued by government entities like NHAI, REC, PFC. Their effective post-tax yield for high-income investors often exceeds comparable taxable bonds.
